newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius fin min sees rupee firmed by economy.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius fin min sees rupee firmed by economy.

text.p: Mauritian Finance Minister Vasant Bunwaree said on Tuesday the strong rupee policy he pledged last week would be achieved by a strengthening economy and not through "artificial means".

"Let me reassure you that we are not going to artificially bring up the value of our currency. This has never been our intention. Our rupee will be strong if our economy is strong," Bunwaree told a delegation of private sector executives.

"We are implementing appropriate macroeconomic policies and bringing about the necessary structural reforms and fiscal discipline to gradually strengthen our economy and therefore help the rupee emerge as a stronger currency," Bunwaree added.
After Bunwaree pledged a strong rupee policy last week, business feared that the export sector in this Indian Ocean island with a small open economy would be seriously undermined.

"In Mauritius, export contracts are usually negotiated several months in advance. A rapid appreciation (of the rupee) would cause tremors in the export enterprises," Francois Woo, chairman of the Mauritius Export Processing Zone Association, told Reuters in reaction to Bunwaree's comments.
